title: folder: similarity merges across a differing bare word and the template shows one member's word (w1p revisited)
description:
Found by the gateway study 2026-08-29 (examples/lab-audit/STUDY_2026-08-29_uxg_gateway.md, per-corpus reports and ##CASE candidates in examples/lab-audit/study-2026-08-29-uxg/).

Similarity merges lines that differ in one or two bare alphabetic words, and the template prints the first member's word. Counted across the gateway corpora: error 27,055 lines (Unreachable+Timeout+Unknown[13] = one group of 19,890; Server Busy+Server Reject = 7,165 with the single Reject invisible), kern 699 (window key setup start|done; ECM init|exit), wan-diag-port 288 (Gained|Lost carrier across 21 interfaces -> 2 groups), wan-diag-ipv6 38 (Adding|Removing route), network-init 14 (Creating bridge|svlan|ethvlan), auth 73 (pam sshd:auth|account; sudo synctime|anonid|restart systemd-timesyncd; a trailing "disconnected by user" dropped), updater 25 (three binary versions hidden in one group of 16; top|bottom phase split 8/1/7), dnscrypt 104 ([TCP]|[UDP]), cron 7 (weekday/tz), messages (ON->OFF vs OFF->ON split while ipv4|ipv6 folds — the outcome depends on word length).

w1p chose (a): the VARIES rollup reports untokenised variation. It does (kern, netinit, updater confirm) — the rollup is truthful, the template is not, and a 1-in-7,165 outcome becomes a footnote. Options: (a) keep; (b) refuse to merge when non-token words differ (rejected at w1p); (c) merge, but print <VARIES> in the template at the differing position. Owner decision; blocked until taken.
close_reason: template shows <VARIES>, rollup counts every variant; merge-refusal measured and rejected

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Done in db41c59. The group keeps a living template: a merged member that differs in a plain word at a position turns that word into <VARIES>, so --explain's normalized, --essence and the --summary key never claim a word half the members lack. The VARIES rollup now counts every member's word and reports sample_counts beside samples, most frequent first and the rarest last: error.log's 19,890-line group reads "reporter_fail(): <VARIES> (<PATH>" with Unreachable 16846 / Timeout 3002 / Unknown[13] 42, and the 7,165 group shows Busy 7164 / Reject 1. Text mode: varies×2 {Busy×7164, Reject×1}.

Option (b), refusing the merge, was implemented and measured first: openssh_brute_force 23 → 5,659 groups, journalctl 2,496 → 8,035, cilium 360 → 1,366 — the differing words are overwhelmingly usernames, hostnames and pod names no detector claims, which an agent needs folded. Reverted. Decision by the CLAUDE.local.md principles: nothing hidden (counts), templates are claims (<VARIES>), bounded (fold counts unchanged: --diff on all 40 corpora, zero moves).

Also in the commit: the klog header pid column is <PID> whatever its digits. Perf single-thread: kubelet +2.8%, cilium +1.5%, journalctl +2.8%.

title: Threshold sweep: optimal default from 85 to 75
description: Swept --threshold values across 16 example logs to find optimal default. The original 85 was a magic number with no empirical basis.
design:
## Methodology

Swept 9 threshold values (50, 60, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100) across 16
example log files, then narrowed to 72-78 range with quality spot-checks.

### Test corpus (16 files)
apache (100), apiserver (4.8k), argocd-controller (28k), argocd-server (61k),
cilium (38k), harbor-postgres-primary (54k), harbor-postgres-replica (24k),
hdfs (100), kubelet (71k), microservices (53), nginx (50), prometheus (100),
rancher (22k), realistic-repetitive (70), security-attacks (64), vllm (3.2k)

## Results

### Wide sweep (avg across 16 files)
| Threshold | Avg Compression | Avg Output Lines |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
| 50% | 88.5% | 52 |
| 60% | 87.6% | 87 |
| 70% | 82.0% | 178 |
| 75% | 80.3% | 197 |
| 80% | 79.9% | 215 |
| 85% | 77.8% | 232 |
| 90% | 75.0% | 252 |
| 100% | 71.5% | 351 |

### Narrow sweep (72-78)
| Threshold | Avg Compression | Avg Output |
|-----------|----------------|------------|
| 72% | 82.0% | 181 |
| 73% | 82.0% | 185 |
| 74% | 80.8% | 191 |
| 75% | 80.3% | 197 |
| 76% | 80.1% | 201 |
| 77% | 79.9% | 206 |
| 78% | 80.0% | 209 |

## Quality cliff at 73

At threshold=73, nginx log merges HTTP 304 and 200 responses into one group.
At 74+, they correctly separate. This is the critical boundary — below 74,
different HTTP status codes (different semantic meaning) get merged.

Security log at 73 merges SSH admin+root attempts. At 74+ they stay separate.

## Key findings by log type

- **HDFS**: 85 splits identical "delete block" ops into 5 groups (by block ID).
  75 correctly merges to 1 group.
- **Prometheus**: Same pattern — "Deleting obsolete block" splits at 85, merges at 75.
- **Security**: All attack types stay properly separated at 75. At 50-60, SSH/SQL/rate-limit bleed together.
- **k8s (kubelet, cilium, rancher)**: 1-2% better compression at 75 with no quality loss.
- **nginx**: Correctly separates status codes at 74+, merges them at 73-.

## Decision
Changed default from 85 → 75. The 85 was a magic number from the first commit
with no testing. 75 gives 3% better avg compression with zero quality regressions.
close_reason: Research complete. Default changed 85→75 in commit b80432c.

title: fix: --summary/--top at --threads 1 silently drop patterns beyond 1000 groups
description:
Verified 2026-08-23 on main 84629ca (0.4.5). Repro: 1,100 mutually dissimilar lines, `--summary --top 0 --threads 1` reports "1000 of 1000 patterns, 1000 of 1100 lines, 91% coverage" — 100 patterns silently evicted and removed from the denominator, so the footer claims completeness it does not have. At 50k unique lines coverage drops to 2% while still claiming "1000 of 1000 patterns". Parallel mode (default) is correct: 50000/50000.

Mechanism: single-thread `process_line` evicts via `flush_oldest_safe_group()` once the buffer exceeds CONSTITUTIONAL_FLUSH_THRESHOLD=1000 (src/folder/mod.rs:1437). Fold mode prints the evicted group; ranked modes (summary/top/fit) ignore the returned string and rank only the remaining buffer. Markdown buffers evictions; JSON emits them as records; only ranked modes lose data, and only at --threads 1.

Fix direction: ranked modes must hold all groups to rank anyway (parallel mode already does exactly this), so gate eviction off when config.summary || config.top_n.is_some() || fit — decided inside the folder from its own Config, NOT via a new main.rs callback (aligns with r98.7 which retires the note_* callback pattern). Check whether --preflight shares the lossy path and include it if so.

Acceptance:
1. The 1,100-unique repro shows 1100 of 1100 patterns at --threads 1; footer numerator and denominator truthful at any cardinality.
2. Fold/JSON/markdown output byte-identical to current behavior (eviction path untouched for streaming modes).
3. Regression test covering ranked-mode retention past 1000 groups at threads=1.
4. src/folder/ change: run the six-corpus compare + bench gate per CLAUDE.md before commit.

Found by the 2026-08-23 lab audit (580 streams, 4.2M lines); audit finding P0-1.

title: sanitizer: keyed pseudonyms so masking preserves the fold
description:
Add a `pseudonym` action alongside `redact`, so a masked value keeps its
identity without keeping its content.

## Why this matters more here than elsewhere

Folding by identity is what lessence is. Flat redaction destroys it: if every
host becomes `<HOST>`, four distinct hosts fold into one group and the rollup
can no longer say there were four. The product's central promise — every unique
thing stays visible — is exactly what redaction breaks.

A stable keyed hash does not. One host becoming `<HOST:a41f>` on every
occurrence means it still groups with itself, `fqdn×3` still reports three
distinct hosts, correlation across lines still works, and the value is gone.
This is the same reasoning behind Cloud DLP's keyed tokenisation and Presidio's
`hash`/`encrypt` operators.

## To decide

1. Keyed or unkeyed. An unkeyed hash of a small space (RFC1918 addresses, short
   hostnames) is trivially reversible by brute force, so a key is the safer
   default — but a key must come from somewhere and be stable across runs for
   the output to stay comparable.
2. Where the key lives: env var, config file, or generated per run. Per run
   makes two runs incomparable, which may be acceptable or may not.
3. Token length. Short enough to read, long enough that collisions stay rare
   within one log.
4. Whether pseudonyms appear in the rollup samples in place of the values.
   They should — that is the whole point — but it changes the sample contract.

## Constraints

1. Determinism is load-bearing in this codebase (see the rand_chacha rationale
   in Cargo.toml): the same input plus the same key must give the same output on
   every platform, or snapshot tests and agent caches break.
2. Off by default.

## Done when

An entity can be pseudonymised instead of redacted, group counts and rollup
distinct-counts are unchanged versus the unmasked run, and the value never
appears in output.

comments.text: Reproduced and quantified on current HEAD; no change shipped (bead says owner approval required). Mechanism: src/patterns/quoted.rs:124-130 collapses any quoted content holding a backslash plus one of : { [ to the opaque <ESCAPED_JSON>, discarding the payload — and it does so immediately after eight detectors have already normalized that same payload into a local normalized_content, which is then thrown away. title: epic: sanitizer entity coverage and keyed pseudonyms
description:
Today `--sanitize-pii` is a boolean covering two entity kinds: emails
(`<EMAIL>`) and credential-class values (`<SECRET>`, `<JWT>`, `<KEY>`). Within
that scope it is careful — it masks the value everywhere it appears, including
inside the rollup variation samples, which is the part most tools get wrong.

The gap is scope and vocabulary, not correctness. Host identifiers and network
addresses are not covered, and the flag has no way to express "cover this kind,
with this treatment". For the tool's stated purpose — handing logs to an LLM or
an agent — those are often exactly the fields an operator would want handled.

Detailed coverage analysis is deliberately not in this tracker; see the local
notes referenced in CLAUDE.local.md.

## What the field does

Verified against the sources 2026-08-25:

1. Microsoft Presidio, open source, the closest analogue.
   https://github.com/microsoft/presidio
   Operators: https://github.com/microsoft/presidio/blob/main/docs/anonymizer/index.md
   Recognizers pair patterns with NER, rule-based logic AND checksum
   validation with surrounding context — the checksum step is what keeps
   false positives down, and is the piece lessence has no equivalent of.
   Anonymizer operators are separate from detection and selectable per entity
   type, with a DEFAULT fallback: replace, redact, hash, encrypt, mask.

2. Google Sensitive Data Protection, formerly Cloud DLP.
   https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/reference/rpc/google.privacy.dlp.v2
   Named infoType taxonomy plus de-identification transforms. Two matter here:
   `CryptoDeterministicConfig`, which the docs recommend where you need
   referential integrity but not to preserve the input alphabet, and
   `CryptoReplaceFfxFpeConfig` for format-preserving encryption. The stated
   guarantee is the one this epic wants: for a given key and context, the same
   identifier is always replaced by the same surrogate. FPE is documented as
   carrying significant latency cost, so deterministic hashing is the cheaper
   route for us.

3. OpenTelemetry Collector `redaction` processor.
   https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/redactionprocessor/README.md
   Allow-list of permitted attribute keys (`allowed_keys`, or `allow_all_keys`
   to disable it) plus a `blocked_values` regex list that masks regardless.
   Non-allowed keys are dropped before any value check. Allow-listing is the
   right default for a high-risk sink.

Named from prior knowledge, NOT re-verified this session — check before
relying on any detail: Elastic ingest `redact` processor, Datadog Sensitive
Data Scanner, Cribl Stream `Mask`. The claim being made about all three is
only the shared shape: a shipped rule library, plus custom rules, plus a
per-rule action.

## The idea worth stealing

Keyed pseudonyms rather than flat redaction. A stable HMAC — one host becoming
`<HOST:a41f>` every time — keeps the fold intact: the same host still groups
with itself, and `fqdn×3` still reports three distinct hosts, while the value
itself is gone. Flat redaction to `<HOST>` throws that grouping away, which for
this tool is throwing away the product. Folding by identity is what lessence
is; a pseudonym preserves identity without preserving the value.

It also resolves a tension with lessence-c2f, which argues for classifying
dotted names LESS: a name that is no longer erased for compression reasons can
be pseudonymised instead of left bare.

## Shape

Entity set `{email, credential, host, ip}`, actions `{redact, pseudonym}`, with
today's behaviour as the default so no existing invocation changes. Deliberately
small: four entities, two actions.

## Sequencing

Design the surface first (child 1). Host and IP coverage (child 2) and keyed
pseudonyms (child 3) both depend on that decision, and child 2 additionally
overlaps lessence-c2f, because masking a host means recognising one.

comments.text:
# Findings: blank/structural lines in --summary and --top N (2026-08-23)

Binary: lessence 0.4.5, built from main @ 84629ca. Evaluation is evidence-only; no product change.

## Q1 — occurrence and slot displacement

Six benchmark corpora (rancher, cilium, harbor_postgres_primary, argocd_server, kubelet, epyc_7days_journalctl):

1. Four of six contain zero blank and zero punctuation-only lines; their summaries have zero noise slots at top-10/20/30.
2. harbor_postgres_primary: one blank line in 54,066 -> one count-1 blank pattern at rank 15 of 72. Displaces one count-1 tail pattern. Negligible.
3. kubelet: 3,108 pure `>` lines (klog `err=<...>` terminator) -> rank 8 of 128. Costs exactly 1 slot of 30 (3.3%). At `--top 10` it displaces a distinct 2,040x pattern ("Error updating node status, will retry") — the strongest real-corpus displacement observed. Note the 5,468x ` > pod="..."` line at rank 5 is a klog continuation WITH content; any rule must not catch it.

Ten blank-heavy corpora (real: GHA CI log of this repo, cargo test --lib output; generated realistic: pytest failures, java stacktraces, python tracebacks, jq-pretty JSON, go test -v, SMTP-session records, YAML multidoc, probe-dot log):

1. Identical blank lines merge into ONE pattern (exact normalized-text merge), so blank lines cost at most 1 slot regardless of volume — but that slot is rank 1 in 7 of 10 corpora, and renders as `[400x] ` with an empty representative, which reads like a rendering bug in the most prominent position.
2. The only multi-slot case is pretty-printed JSON: 7 distinct punctuation-only fragments (`{`, `}`, `},`, `]`, ...) occupy 7 of 30 slots (23%); top-10 useful-line coverage is 53.8% vs 76.9% if demoted.
3. Whitespace-only variants do NOT merge: `""`, `"\t"`, `"   "` are three separate patterns, all rendering as identical blank rows — mixed blank styles can occupy several slots.
4. GHA CI logs are immune: every line carries the job/step/timestamp prefix, so blank source lines never reach the folder as blank.

## Q2 — missed useful patterns

Displacement puts a useful pattern out of the window only when total patterns exceed the cap. Measured displaced patterns were count-1 tail singletons in every fixture (yaml, pytest, gotest) except kubelet `--top 10` (2,040x pattern lost, above) and pretty JSON (7 comparable-value fragments). At default `--top 30`, no corpus lost a pattern with count > 1 except kubelet (211x) and json_pretty (50x).

## Q3 — when blank/structural lines carry information

1. Record-delimited logs (SMTP fixture): the blank count IS the record count (400 blanks = 400 sessions); nothing else in the log states it.
2. YAML multidoc: `---` count = document count (500).
3. Probe-dot logs: `.` x 2,925 IS the signal (successes between failures); suppressing it collapses coverage from 100% to 2.5%.
4. kubelet `>`: redundant — the error bodies it terminates already hold ranks 1–3.
5. Adjacency-based meaning (blank separating stack-trace blocks) exists only in default fold mode; summary mode has no adjacency, so that argument does not apply to ranking changes scoped to summary display.

## Q4 — de-prioritization vs filtering

Simulated three strategies on all corpora (script recorded in repro comment): current (count order), demote (patterns whose representative contains no alphanumeric character sort last; nothing removed), filter (such rows removed).

1. Demote and filter produce byte-identical bounded windows whenever patterns overflow the cap. They differ only when everything fits — exactly where there is no slot pressure — and there filter destroys information (probe dots, session counts) while demote keeps it visible at the bottom. Demote strictly dominates filter.
2. Demotion gains: kubelet top-10 +1 useful pattern (+3.1pp useful-line coverage); pretty JSON top-10 +3 patterns (+23.1pp); all other corpora +0.1 to +3.5pp. Small everywhere except pretty JSON.
3. Demotion harm case, quantified: a punctuation-only pattern that is the dominant signal in a log with more patterns than the cap would leave the bounded window (declared by the "N of M patterns" stderr line, but invisible). Not observed in any real corpus here — probe-dot logs have few patterns and stay visible under demotion — but it is the failure mode to weigh.
4. A format-agnostic rule suffices: "trimmed representative contains no alphanumeric character". It needs no per-format heuristics, catches ``, `>`, `---`, `.`, `{`, and correctly excludes ` > pod="..."`, `250 2.0.0 accepted`, and short meaningful lines like `OK`/`FAIL` (alphanumeric). Blank is a subset of the rule.

## Q5 — preservation promise

1. Input filtering violates zero-data-loss outright (breaks default fold mode and the probe-dot corpus) — ruled out.
2. Display filtering omits undeclared information in the no-overflow case — conflicts with "anything omitted is declared" unless a new declaration line is added.
3. Ranking-only demotion omits nothing: with `--top 0` everything is still shown; bounded views already omit declared amounts. Only candidate compatible with the promise.

## Conclusion (per acceptance criteria)

Evidence is real but small: on the primary corpora the cost of current behavior is at most 1 slot of 30 plus a confusing blank rank-1 row on blank-heavy logs; the one materially bad shape is pretty-printed JSON (23% of slots). Harm from suppression is demonstrated (probe dots, record counts), which rules out filtering entirely. Per criterion 5, current behavior is retained. If the owner wants improvement, display-only demotion under the no-alphanumeric rule is the only candidate compatible with the preservation promise, and it should be a separate owner-approved bead. Fixture bias note: the ten extra corpora deliberately over-sample blank-heavy formats; the six primary corpora are nearly blank-free.

title: Fix non-char-boundary panic in --summary line truncation
description:
src/folder.rs:1013 — format_summary_line truncates a representative line with the byte-index slice &representative[..avail]. avail is byte-derived (width.saturating_sub(prefix.len()+3)) and the avail>20 guard does not align it to a UTF-8 char boundary. representative is untrusted log content (group.first().original.clone(), folder.rs:950).

Impact: a log line longer than the terminal width with a multibyte char (emoji/CJK/accented) straddling byte offset avail panics ("byte index is not a char boundary"). With panic = abort (Cargo.toml) the whole process aborts. Triggered on a TTY in --summary / --fit / --human. Concrete trigger: width 80, prefix "[3x] ", avail 72; 71 ASCII bytes then a multibyte char at byte 72.

Fix:
1. Truncate on char boundaries, e.g. representative.chars().take(n).collect(), or snap with is_char_boundary before slicing.
2. Prefer truncating by display columns (unicode-width) to keep width accounting correct.
3. Add a regression test with a multibyte char straddling the truncation offset (existing tests use only ASCII).

Provenance: threat-model -> vuln-scan -> triage pipeline; confirmed TRUE_POSITIVE 3/0, confidence 9.0/10; severity MEDIUM. See TRIAGE.md (F-003).

title: normalize: a quoted sentence is the event, not a variable — the 25-char rule erases it
description:
Found by the 25-corpus study (2026-08-28). Largest defect by lines affected.

An unclaimed quoted string over 25 characters is replaced whole by
<QUOTED_STRING> (src/patterns/quoted.rs, the length rule that lessence-8jb
deliberately left in place for "prose"). When that string is the `msg` of a
structured record, the event identity vanishes:

1. argocd_server_production: 59,948 of 60,849 lines (98.5%) in ONE group —
   TLS reload (53,942) + cache-invalidate -cm (2,998) + -secret (2,998) +
   "Notifying subscribers" (2) + 9 one-off startup lines.
2. argocd_controller_production: "Loading TLS configuration" (22,527) merged
   with "Ignore status for all objects" (1,199); "Refreshing app status" (748)
   merged with "Skipping auto-sync" (225).
3. k8s_json_sample: 5 distinct argocd verbs in one group of 138.
4. epyc_7days_journalctl: rke2 logrus — 8+ event types (startup banner,
   tunnel, load balancer, mirror, P2P) in one group of 492.
5. rancher_production: telemetry "Failed to get X" — 8 resource kinds in 1.

The rule is backwards. "Update successful" (17 chars) stays literal and gets
its own group; "Loading TLS configuration from secret argocd/..." (58 chars)
becomes noise. Short messages become the identity and long ones become
variables — the opposite of what a message is.

## Acceptance

A quoted string containing whitespace is a sentence. Tokenise INSIDE it —
numbers, names, paths, timestamps — and keep its words, exactly as an
unquoted sentence is treated. The 25-char rule is deleted. Whether a quoted
value folds never depends on its length.

Measured expectation on argocd_server_production: 4 groups → ~14, with the
59,948 group splitting into TLS (53,942) / cache-cm (2,998) / cache-secret
(2,998) / ... exactly per the study's ground truth.

Gate with --diff against the previous binary on all 25 corpora; every moved
line must be in the splitting direction on a `msg`-shaped field.

Corpus: tests/fixtures/fold_regressions.log ##TODO study-quoted-sentence-is-the-event.
Study reports: the job dir for this session; synthesis is SYNTHESIS.md there.

title: normalize: whether a field value folds depends on its length, not its meaning
description:
Reported by the kubelookout session 2026-08-25, then measured on its real
corpus. Reproduces on the installed 0.4.5 and on the current dev branch; not
fixed by anything unreleased.

Whether a structured-log field value folds depends on the LENGTH of the value,
not on what it means. Short values stay literal and get one template each;
longer ones collapse to `<QUOTED_STRING>` and fold. Two pods logging the same
event shape therefore behave differently based on how long their names happen
to be.

## Root cause

`src/patterns/quoted.rs`, end of `normalize_quoted`: a quoted string that no
detector claimed is replaced with `<QUOTED_STRING>` only when
`quoted_string.len() > 25`, on the reasoning that "only very long strings are
likely variable names". Below that it is returned verbatim.

Demonstrated with one field and five values, `--min-collapse 3`:

    "redis"                          (7 chars)  -> literal, own group
    "redis-sentinel"                (16 chars)  -> literal, own group
    "redis-sentinel-gitlab"         (23 chars)  -> literal, own group
    "redis-sentinel-gitlab-prod"    (28 chars)  -> <QUOTED_STRING> ┐ folded
    "redis-sentinel-gitlab-prod-eu" (31 chars)  -> <QUOTED_STRING> ┘ together

The cutoff is arbitrary with respect to meaning. Renaming an application from
`redis-sentinel-gitlab` to `redis-sentinel-gitlab-prod` changes whether its log
lines fold.

## Scale, measured on a real cluster

kubelookout measured a 15-minute snapshot, 122 pods, 32,730 lines:

1. 29 pods JSON-dominant, 27% of all lines (8,983).
2. Fold survival (lines_out/lines_in, pods with >=20 lines): 7% for JSON pods
   versus 2% for text pods. So folding is degraded about 3.5x on JSON sources,
   NOT disabled — exact-duplicate lines still fold trivially, and some of their
   JSON carries whitespace.
3. Worst offenders are all JSON: tetragon-l5cw4 55% survive, gitlab-gitaly-0
   30%, argocd-application-controller-0 29%, tetragon-fbkw6 28%.
4. Their cross-sweep novelty diff is dominated by argocd and tetragon JSON
   churn, which is this bug surfacing downstream.

An earlier claim in this bead that lessence is "close to a no-op" on compact
JSON was wrong and is retracted; 3.5x degradation is the measured figure.

## Fixture

632 real lines from argocd-application-controller-0, tetragon-fbkw6 and
gitlab-gitaly-0, scrubbed by kubelookout, saved as
`examples/k8s_json_sample.log` (gitignored, and `examples/` is excluded from
the crate). Sections are marked `##### ns/name`. A second copy is at
`~/lessence-fixtures/k8s_json_sample.log`.

Measured on it with `--format json --sanitize-pii --min-collapse 3 --threads 1`:
218 groups from 634 lines, 155 of them singletons. Note the line-length profile
is bimodal — p50 is 270 bytes, p90 is 29.5 KB — because tetragon emits very
large records.

Real argocd lines fold better than the synthetic repro first filed here
suggested, because their `msg` and `application` values happen to exceed 25
characters. That is the bug, not a mitigation.

## Secondary effect

Similarity cannot compensate once values stay literal.
`SimTokens::from_normalized` splits on whitespace, and compact JSON has none,
so the whole line is ONE token and the LCS score against a sibling is 0. Adding
spaces does not rescue it either:

    {"a":"x1","b":"same","c":"same"}     -> no fold (1 token)
    {"a":"x1", "b":"same", "c":"same"}   -> no fold (3 tokens, 1 differs = 66%)

Both sit under the default threshold of 83. So raising the threshold or tuning
similarity cannot substitute for tokenizing the values.

## Suggested acceptance

Field values in JSON and logfmt records are tokenized on the same basis
regardless of their length, so that four lines differing only in a field value
fold into one group on both the compact-JSON and logfmt shapes at
`--min-collapse 3` and the default threshold.

Whatever replaces the 25-character rule should be defensible in terms of the
field, its key, or its variability — not the incidental length of one value.

Gate as usual, and use the new fixture: the existing `examples/` corpora are
mostly plaintext, which is why this went unnoticed.

## Downstream

kubelookout keys a persistent template store on exact `normalized` output plus
a lessence build column, so the size of their template inventory is decided by
this bead. They flagged it as one of two things they want from lessence, the
other being the git-commit-in-version change reaching an installed release.
close_reason: field values fold on shape (DNS-1123 identifier) and JSON numbers at any digit count

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Fixed in 2632344 and 92ea725. Two rules, one cause: the code guessed "long
enough means variable" in two places, so folding depended on the incidental
length of a value.

1. `src/patterns/quoted.rs` — an unclaimed quoted string became
   `<QUOTED_STRING>` only past 25 characters. Replaced by a shape recogniser
   of the same kind every other detector already is: a whole-value DNS-1123
   identifier (no whitespace, lowercase, carrying a hyphen or a digit) folds
   at any length. Nothing looks at keys or key vocabularies.

2. `src/patterns/duration.rs` — integers folded only at three digits or more,
   a floor that exists so prose like "3 retries" survives. A number that is
   the whole value of a JSON field now folds at any digit count. This turned
   out to be the larger half: an argocd reconciliation record carries about
   thirty `_ms` fields, so every one of those lines stood alone.

The plan this started from was wrong and was scrapped. It proposed reading the
key next to the value and keeping a list of "identity" fields (level, msg,
severity) whose values would not fold. The owner rejected it: nothing about
this needs to be different from how every other pattern is handled. Recognise
the shape, emit a token, done.

## The limit, stated deliberately

A bare word does not fold. `"info"`, `"default"`, `"argocd"`, `"harbor"` and
this bead's own `"redis"` are shape-identical to an enum value, and nothing on
the line separates an app named redis from a log level named info except the
key beside it. Four of the bead's five example values fold; `"redis"` does
not. That is the price of not reading keys, and it is cheap: on the fixture
only two of fifteen varying values are bare words.

## What the placeholder had to be

The new rule emits `<QUOTED_STRING>`, not a new token. Measured: any other
placeholder leaves short and long values of the same field in different groups
and the bug survives. On the eight argocd "Update successful" groups, a new
placeholder gives 3 groups; `<QUOTED_STRING>` gives 1.

## One byte of lookahead, for keys only

A JSON key has the same shape as an instance name. The shape fold is vetoed
when the byte after the closing quote is a colon, which keeps the record's
schema in the template. Two paired tests prove the veto is positional and not
baked into the memo cache.

## logfmt numbers were measured and rejected

Extending rule 2 to bare `key=42` was built and measured. auditd SYSCALL
records carry around forty numeric fields, so folding all of them pushed
records for different syscalls past the similarity threshold and merged them:
linux_auditd 649 output lines to 344, with modprobe/kmod records absorbed into
an ntpd group. The JSON-only form carries the entire measured win with zero
effect on linux_auditd and cilium_full. Shipped JSON-only, deliberately, with
a test pinning it.

## Measured

Fixture `examples/k8s_json_sample.log`, 634 lines,
`--format json --sanitize-pii --min-collapse 3 --threads 1`:
groups 140 to 26, singletons 105 to 6, distinct normalized templates 140 to 26.

Head-to-head against an unmodified HEAD build, default flags, all 25 corpora.
Output line counts:

1. argocd_controller_production 977 to 30
2. k8s_json_sample 205 to 63
3. kubelet 494 to 485
4. rancher_production 298 to 292
5. epyc_7days_journalctl 3229 to 3225
6. realistic_repetitive 44 to 42
7. every remaining corpus unchanged in line count

Rule 1 alone accounts for 977 to 929 and 205 to 156; rule 2 for the rest.

Nothing regressed. Sixteen corpora are byte-identical. The corpora that show a
text diff without a line-count change are all rollup annotations gaining a
value they previously baked into the template, e.g. linux_auditd now reports
`quoted_string×1 {"ip6tables"}` on a group whose membership did not move.
Every plaintext corpus (apache, nginx, hdfs, openssh, auth_secure,
kubectl_events, synthetic, harbor) is untouched by both rules.

## A note on the reference sweep

`examples/references/tools/compare.sh examples/references/v0.4.1` reports
PASS=21 FAIL=147, but an unmodified HEAD build produces the same plaintext
diffs — the v0.4.1 reference set is stale relative to HEAD and cannot judge
this change. All gating above was done head-to-head against a HEAD build
instead. The reference set wants refreshing, separately.

## Perf

Six corpora, `taskset -c 0-13`, threads 8, 3 alternating runs against the
unmodified HEAD binary: all within noise. The 73 MB journalctl corpus is
faster (base 15.70/13.39/13.77s, new 11.84/13.30/12.31s) because there are
fewer groups to scan. `make ci` green.

## Follow-ups, not done here

1. A quoted JSON key longer than 25 characters still folds to
   `<QUOTED_STRING>` via the untouched length rule, so
   `"set_app_managed_resources_ms"` vanishes from the template. Pre-existing,
   not what this bead reported.
2. Bare unquoted logfmt string values (`subsys=config`) remain
   KeyValueDetector's hardcoded allowlist. Separate risk, separate change.
3. The v0.4.1 reference outputs are stale.

title: folder: repeated patterns fragment into multiple group records across evictions
description: Audit finding P1-4: 84,329 lines across 300 repeated normalized keys emitted as 664 separate group records in streamed fold/JSON output. Cause is the same streaming eviction mechanism as lessence-2dr: an evicted group's key can re-form a new group later. Distinct from the ranked-mode bug (streamed modes legitimately evict); candidate fix is merging completed groups by normalized key before rendering, or tracking last-update position. Owner decision on whether the streaming tradeoff is worth changing.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Investigated with measurements; no code change shipped. Reproduced on epyc_7days_journalctl at --threads 1 --format json: 1682 group records for 1585 distinct keys, 97 keys emitted twice, 228250 lines affected. Default parallel mode emits 1532 records with zero splits, confirming streaming eviction as the cause. Findings on the two candidate fixes named in this issue: 1. Tracking last-update position DOES NOT WORK. Implemented it (evict only groups untouched for safe_distance, oldest-created first, LRU fallback), and fragmentation stayed at exactly 97 keys while the output changed. The splits are dominated by periodic patterns such as hourly cron, which are quiet under any threshold and get evicted between occurrences. Reverted. 2. Merging completed groups by normalized key before rendering is not available in streaming mode, because records are written as they are evicted; there is no pre-render point. Capacity is the real lever but is not removable. With eviction effectively disabled, fragmentation goes to zero and the six real corpora cost at most 5 percent more memory (711 MB to 751 MB on journalctl) and run slightly faster. However the buffer cap also bounds the linear similarity scan in cluster_line_at, and on a high-cardinality input (67k mutually dissimilar lines) removing it takes the run from 5.0 s to 187.9 s. The cap must stay. Remaining viable option, needs owner decision: keep the evicted key in group_index mapped to the record id it was emitted as, and re-emit a re-formed group under that same id so JSONL consumers can merge. Costs O(distinct keys) of (u64, usize) — about 1500 entries on this corpus — leaves the similarity scan untouched, and is a JSONL schema change that does not help text mode.

title: report all skipped capped and omitted data in JSON
description:
Agent consumers must be able to distinguish a complete lessence result from one where input, groups, or variable values were intentionally omitted. Current omission mechanisms include `--top`, the summary cap, `--max-lines`, `--max-line-length`, `--fit`, and per-token rollup caps, but there is no single machine-readable completeness contract.

## Required Behavior

1. Define every path that can skip, cap, truncate, sample, or omit information.
2. Add machine-readable JSON metadata stating whether the result is complete.
3. Report omission counts by reason wherever exact counts are available.
4. Mark lower bounds and unknown counts explicitly rather than presenting them as exact.
5. Preserve the existing per-variation `capped` signal and make its relationship to document-level completeness clear.
6. Do not claim completeness when processing stopped early or output was bounded.
7. Keep stdout valid JSONL in every flag combination.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. JSON consumers can determine whether all input lines were processed.
2. JSON consumers can determine whether all groups were emitted.
3. JSON consumers can determine whether variation values were capped or sampled.
4. Tests cover `--top`, summary caps, `--max-lines`, overlong lines, `--fit`, and rollup caps.
5. The JSON schema documents exact, lower-bound, and unknown omission counts.
6. Existing unbounded folding behavior and text output remain unchanged unless explicitly documented and approved.

The JSON schema documents exact, lower-bound, and unknown omission counts. 6. Existing unbounded folding behavior and text output remain unchanged unless explicitly documented and approved.

comments.author: codex
comments.text:
Implemented a machine-readable completeness contract for JSONL output.

1. Summary records now report document, input, group, and variation-value completeness.
2. Every omission count is explicitly exact, lower_bound, or unknown.
3. Input metadata covers --max-lines, overlong lines, and failed sources.
4. Group metadata covers --top, the JSON --summary default cap, and --fit.
5. Variation entries expose exact/lower-bound distinct counts, sample completeness, and omitted sample counts; the summary aggregates caps, sampling, and groups whose rollup was not computed.
6. --summary/--fit combined with --format json now remains valid JSONL.
7. README and the JSON schema document the contract and stdin/limit semantics.
8. Focused JSON tests passed (24 tests). Full CI passed 1,317 tests; cargo deny passed separately after the sandbox blocked its advisory lock. No text-output or unbounded folding behavior was changed.

title: hosts and cluster study: template honesty, anchors, token shapes
description:
Second corpus study of 2026-08-29: 5 switch/AP, 6 host and 30 cluster corpora (`examples/usw_*`, `uap_*`, `host_*`, `nas_dmesg`, `k8s_*`), 41 files, ~2.3 M lines, 24 Sonnet agents. Synthesis in `examples/lab-audit/STUDY_2026-08-29_hosts_k8s.md`, reports in `study-2026-08-29-hosts-k8s/`.

Seventeen defect classes, grouped by principle (see the synthesis). This bead tracks the fixes; each commit names the classes it closes.

1. Template honesty: placeholder-vs-word and unequal-length positions never became `<VARIES>`; `key=` prefixes lost; two VARIES slots merged opposite outcomes.
2. Anchors: kubectl prefix, structured caller, message call site, traceback frame, HTTP method/status/route fields, digest route segments.
3. Wrong tokens: `<PID>` on any `[N]`, `<PORT>` on any `word:NN`, `<FQDN>` on facility.level, asctime weekday, dmesg uptime width, bracketed epoch glued to a word, 16-digit epoch as hash, partial multi-unit durations, quote-swallowing durations, designator suffixes, DT addresses, `request:` prose as request id, execID, `\x2d` UUIDs, program tag as path, tetragon key-value gates.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Batch 1 (template honesty and anchors), measured on all 65 corpora against 9124ec7.

Template: a placeholder against a plain word now varies; members of another word count are LCS-aligned and the words they lack vary (counted as ∅); a shared field name stays in front (`msg=<VARIES>`, `"NodeName":<VARIES>`); a quoted value with spaces is one slot. Words are split at `,` `{` `}` outside quotes, so a spaceless JSON record is its fields (argocd 189→52, postgres-operator 169→92, etcd 84→70, gitlab 347→319 groups).

Join refusal: a line differing from a group's founder in two or more sentence words founds its own group (redis sync/lost, sentinel +sdown/+reboot, events SuccessfulCreate/Delete, scheduler watch/list, Fork CoW RDB/AOF). Cost in groups: kubelet 229→249, cilium 361→379, epyc journal 2512→2574 (systemd unit descriptions), openssh 23→32 (distinct sshd messages), auditd 418→434 (success=yes/no).

Anchors: kubectl `[pod/<pod>/<container>]` (container + pod skeleton: replicas, ordinals, osd-N, mon-xx fold; workloads do not — vllm health 4 deployments, rook 2303→2350), structured `caller`, klog message call site (openebs 59→75), Python traceback frame (grafana 38→50), JSON/logfmt method + status class + route (traefik 20→605: 557 distinct routes, the Apache-shape rule applied to JSON), `sha256:` digest route segments (harbor 421→222), RPC method names.

`host:port` only for dotted hosts or localhost: `count:26`, `size:107`, `Threshold:80`, `CacheBlockSize:1600` stay fields.

Perf, single-thread pinned, median of 3 interleaved: kubelet 5.38→5.39 s (+0.2%), cilium 2.25→2.29 s (+1.9%), epyc journal 18.06→18.02 s (−0.2%), rook-ceph 9.53→9.42 s (−1.2%).

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Batch 2 (timestamps, hashes, small integers), measured on all 65 corpora against 6ffb87c.

asctime (`Sat Aug 29 08:40:15 2026`, Apache `[Sat … .123456 2026]`, git `Aug 29 … 2026`) now outranks syslog-bsd: uap_messages 177→139, apache_error 70→48, uxg_messages 73→59. The kernel uptime stamp `[    0.028586]` / `[4324019.474441]` is one `<TIMESTAMP>` whatever its width (nas_dmesg's snapshot group rejoined). A bracket glued to a word (`trace[1539274761]`, `Trace[…]:`) is an index, not an epoch. A 16-digit number starting with 1 is an epoch in microseconds; fixed-width hex runs made of digits alone are numbers, not hashes.

Two small integers match each other in the similarity metric (the line still shows them: `GPS mode <VARIES> -> <VARIES>` with counts): host_pi_journal 208→185, hdfs 12→9, uxg_kern 262→237, epyc journal 2574→2542. The dmesg corpora grow (usw_dmesg 296→336, nas_dmesg 656→691): `[    <DECIMAL>]` used to count as two matching tokens, which let `TC init (unit 0)` fold with `Watchdog init (unit 0)` — different subsystems, an accidental fold, now honestly apart.

Under `--sanitize-pii` a VARIES value is counted in its masked form; the slot had dropped the `password=` the mask keys on, and the raw values reached the rollup once short lines folded (caught by the security suite).

Perf, single-thread pinned, median of 3 interleaved: kubelet 5.38→5.46 s (+1.4%), cilium 2.29→2.31 s (+0.7%), epyc journal 17.99→18.20 s (+1.2%), host_pi_journal 0.36→0.37 s.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Batch 3 (token shapes), measured on all 65 corpora against 7dd3577.

A bracketed number is a pid only in a syslog tag (`sshd[1234]:`), a leading `[1234]` or a `[pid=N]` field; `slot[2]`, `sta_cnt[5]`, `GENPLL[5]`, `round[1]`, `disk[0]`, `FWLOG: [N]` and `id=N` stay what they are. A single dash before a word is a sign, not a flag (`-sdown`). Letters-then-digits is a designator (`ssh-ed25519`), not a generated suffix, unless drawn from the k8s generated alphabet (`tsd92`). `3f00b880.mailbox` is an `<ADDR>`. `request: tokenreviews` is prose, not a request id. A syslog program tag written as a path stays whole (`/usr/libexec/xdg-desktop-portal[<PID>]:`). `daemon.info` is the facility.level field, not a domain.

A quoted string of more than three words is a sentence and its words stay their own units — batch 1 had made the whole kubelet message one `<VARIES>` when a value inside it differed. A bracketed value (`volumes=[valkey-data]`) is a value, and a word the other line carries elsewhere is a repetition, not a new sentence word (a list that grew by one entry). Tokens ending in a small integer with equal surroundings match each other (`slot[1]`/`slot[2]`, `id=1`/`id=2`, `ses=1`/`ses=3`, `08:24`/`08:39`) and the template shows `slot[<VARIES>]` with counts: linux_auditd 435→172, rook-ceph 2338→678, cilium 379→350, host_fedora_journal 1763→1727, uxg_updater 52→41, k8s_gitlab 319→307; kubelet 248→254 (`[N]` no longer a pid in Go struct dumps).

Perf, single-thread pinned, median of 3 interleaved: kubelet 5.45→5.54 s (+1.8%), cilium 2.30→2.35 s (+2.1%), epyc journal 18.34→18.82 s (+2.6%), linux_auditd 0.26→0.25 s.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
HANDOFF 2026-08-29 (context exhausted mid batch 3b; tree is dirty, nothing lost).

Uncommitted in the working tree, all unit tests (1139) and the fixture suite passing: spaced multi-unit durations + µs, bare-unit sizes (775.5M, 256Mi), \x2d-escaped UUIDs, id-named JSON fields ("execID":"…", base64 ok), key-value gate on an UNQUOTED '=' (has_unquoted_eq in normalize.rs) with the if/for/while/SELECT vetoes dropped, klog header prefilter for any month (has_klog_header), program-field anchor (exe=, comm=, "binary":). --diff vs batch-3 base (lessence-base = 48d7dcb build): tetragon 569→125, k8s_json_sample 116→70, auditd 172→224, argocd 52→41; last full diff file $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/diff-c3e.txt (may be stale for tetragon/json_sample/auditd — rerun those three).

To finish batch 3b: make docs; cargo test --tests --no-fail-fast; perf.sh kubelet cilium_full epyc_7days_journalctl (alone; $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/perf.sh); make ci; br comments add lessence-a8t; RELEASE_COMMIT=1 git commit (fix:). Then batch 4: syslog <HOST> positional token (after <TIMESTAMP> at line start, before facility.level or tag[pid]:, not all-caps, followed by a tag ending in ':'), the 40-format timestamp corpus, and the final report to the owner. Residual noted: "binary":"<PATH>" hides the program on the line (anchor works, display does not).

Lesson: run builds/diffs/probes in subagents from the start; the main context should hold summaries only.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text:
Batch 3b (durations, sizes, ids, key-value gating, program anchors), measured on all 79 corpora in examples/ against 48d7dcb.

A spaced multi-unit duration (`3d 12h 48min 21.967s`) and a µs value read as one `<DURATION>`; a bare-unit size (`775.5M`, `256Mi`) is one `<SIZE>`. A `\x2d`-escaped UUID inside a systemd unit name is recognised. An id-named JSON field (`"execID":"003d3"`, base64 values included) folds as an id. The key-value detector is gated on an unquoted `=` (`has_unquoted_eq` in normalize.rs) and the old `if `/`for `/`while `/`SELECT ` word vetoes are gone, so tetragon JSON events fold. The klog header prefilter accepts any month (`has_klog_header`). Program fields (`exe=`, `comm=`, `"binary":`) are anchors: matched, never scored.

Groups moved on 15 corpora: k8s_tetragon 569→125, k8s_json_sample 116→70, linux_auditd 172→224, k8s_argocd_aux 52→41, k8s_rook_ceph 678→665, host_fedora_journal 1727→1719, host_fedora_user_journal 1355→1347, epyc journal 2516→2510, k8s_gitlab 307→314, host_rke2_journal 457→453, uxg_dmesg_boot 303→298, microservices 24→21, k8s_kube_state_metrics 33→32, k8s_postgres_operator 92→91, k8s_traefik 605→606; k8s_etcd stays 63 with 4 lines moved. In tetragon and k8s_json_sample every join is same-event: exec and exit stay apart, runc and containerd-shim stay apart, and no binary name or event type appears inside any varies set (base or new). linux_auditd splits by comm/exe: the iptables SYSCALL group 314→156 with ip6tables founding its own 158, auditctl 45→9, the failed execve group 117→49.

Two joins cross an event boundary and are open. In k8s_argocd_aux, `git cat-file -t <sha>` (65 lines) and `git checkout --force <sha>` (59 lines) now share one shown line, rollup `varies×2 {cat-file×65, checkout×59}`; the base kept them apart as 86 and 38. In linux_auditd three SYSCALL connect groups (sudo twice, pkttyagent once) now hold `success=yes exit=0` members beside `success=no exit=-2`, rollups `no×10, yes×3`, `no×4, yes×1`, `no×2, yes×1`; the base had no yes/no-mixed group. Both appear once the execID id and the exe/comm anchors remove every other difference, leaving one word (the git subcommand, the yes/no value) and the one-word-apart rule folds it.

Perf, single-thread pinned, median of 3 interleaved: kubelet 5.60→6.02 s (+7.6%), cilium 2.36→2.39 s (+1.3%), epyc journal 18.96→18.84 s (−0.6%). Unit 1139 green; integration green (the misc target, which holds the fold-scaling and detection-performance tests, failed once under full-suite load and passed 57/57 alone); make ci green; make docs changed nothing.

title: normalize: dotted names are classified by shape, not by evidence
description:
Consolidates lessence-5m4, lessence-c2f, and the third class of lessence-gho.
Those were three symptoms of one cause, each filed from the vantage point of
whoever noticed it, before anyone had diagnosed it:

- 5m4 saw the output ("my error text became `<ESCAPED_JSON>`") and blamed
  `src/patterns/quoted.rs`.
- c2f saw the Kubernetes side ("resource names come out wrong") and blamed the
  k8s/normalize path.
- gho class 3 saw the grouping ("different resources merged") and blamed the
  similarity code.

The cause is in a fourth file. `src/patterns/network.rs:231` decides whether a
dotted token is a hostname by testing its last label against a hardcoded
`COMMON_TLDS` list, and erases it to `<FQDN>` when it matches. Kubernetes names
its API resources in reverse DNS by design, so a resource type is syntactically
indistinguishable from a hostname:

    cephclusters.ceph.rook.io    ends .io  -> on the list  -> erased
    postgresqls.acid.zalan.do    ends .do  -> not listed   -> survives

Two names of the same kind, opposite fates, by coincidence rather than design.

## Evidence

Confirmed by running the RBAC corpus with `--disable-patterns network`: all four
resources reappear intact. One 5,208-line group hides four distinct denials —
cephclusters.ceph.rook.io 2144, postgresqls.acid.zalan.do 1992,
drivers.csi.ceph.io 804, cephobjectstores.ceph.rook.io 268 — plus two distinct
`msg` values.

Blast radius is small where it is currently visible: only 12 output lines across
all 24 standard `examples/` corpora carry `<FQDN>` at all. The existing reference
sweep therefore cannot gate a change here; new fixtures from the lab corpora are
needed.

## Options

1. Keep a list. Add Kubernetes API-group patterns to the vocabulary. Works
   immediately; this is what Drain3 ships as `masking_instructions`, so it is the
   industry norm. Costs perpetual maintenance and is never complete.
2. Give Kubernetes resources their own detector and token. Cleanest result,
   closest to what this bead originally asked for, and to SemParser's
   concept/instance idea (ICSE 2023). Much the largest piece of work.
3. Close and accept the loss.
4. Stop classifying dotted names by shape. Erase a dotted token only on positive
   evidence that it is a network endpoint (a port, a URL scheme, a dial/connect
   verb). Grafana Loki runs this at scale — its Drain tokenizer deliberately does
   not even split on `.` `:` `/`, so it has no hostname detector to get wrong, and
   marks a token variable only by observing that it varies at that position.
   Smallest diff of the options that change anything. Loki's job is not identical
   (per-stream patterns over 3h windows, labels already separating streams), so it
   is not a straight transplant, and genuine hostnames in prose would stop folding.

Recommendation on file: 4, then 1 only where real logs show gaps, so the list
starts empty and grows from evidence instead of starting wrong.

## Prior art

Log template extraction is a mature field and this is its central problem.
All links checked 2026-08-25.

Evaluation and benchmark:

1. A Large-Scale Evaluation for Log Parsing Techniques: How Far Are We?
   Jiang et al., ISSTA 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10828
   15 parsers over Loghub-2.0 (14 datasets, ~3.6M lines each). Finds rare
   events are where parsers still fail, which is exactly the case in this
   bead, and separates grouping accuracy from parsing accuracy because a
   parser can group correctly while still getting the template wrong.

Shape-based masking, which is what lessence does today:

2. Drain3. https://github.com/logpai/Drain3
   Ships `masking_instructions`: user-supplied domain regexes for IPs,
   numbers, UUIDs. Hand-maintained domain knowledge is the state of the
   practice, so option 1 above is the industry norm, not a shortcut.

Evidence-based marking, which is option 4:

3. Grafana Loki's Drain tokenizer.
   https://github.com/grafana/loki/blob/main/pkg/pattern/drain/line_tokenizer.go
   `newPunctuationTokenizer` explicitly EXCLUDES `_ - . : /` from the
   delimiter set, so `cephclusters.ceph.rook.io` stays one atomic token and
   is never classified at all. A token becomes `<_>` only because the tree
   observed it varying at that position — see `pkg/pattern/drain/drain.go`,
   `ParamString`. Read from source 2026-08-25.
   Docs: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/visualizations/simplified-exploration/logs/patterns/
   Caveat: Loki's job is not identical — per-stream patterns over 3h windows,
   with labels already separating streams before Drain runs.

Semantic direction, which is option 2:

4. SemParser, Huo et al., ICSE 2023. https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12636
   Mines concept/instance pairs, so a token is understood as an instance of a
   concept rather than matched on shape. Closest published work to option 2.
5. LogPTR, variable-aware parsing with a pointer network.
   https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.05986
6. VarParser, on variables carrying meaning rather than being noise.
   https://arxiv.org/html/2601.22676v1

## Interaction to watch

This pulls in the opposite direction from the sanitizer epic: option 4 reduces
how much lessence classifies, while masking a host for privacy requires
recognising it first. Decide the two together.

comments.text: Scoped, not implemented (bead says owner approval required). The r98.4 sequencing precondition it names is now satisfied — that bead is closed and the timestamp registry it refers to has since been collapsed entirely (lessence-vvk). Measurement on the flagship kubelet corpus: only 231 of 70548 lines carry a literal slash-delimited object reference in a folded representative, and 27 carry a literal resource quantity; several of the 231 are false positives from my matcher catching net/http rather than a namespace/name reference. K8S_NAME covers 5667/70548 lines across 17/179 groups. So on the standard corpora this finding is close to absent; the audit's counts (4065 quantities, 16732 k8sPodName, 10969 object references) come from the 580-file lab-audit sweep. The blocker is not size but specification: 'context-aware quantity and object-reference handling' does not say what should change, and separating K8S_NAME from K8S_NAMESPACE is a normalized-output change affecting every kubernetes user. Recommend the owner either state the intended normalized forms concretely or close this as covered by the anchor work, since the object-reference half overlaps the resource-name anchor class still open on lessence-gho. comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Merging this with lessence-5m4 and the open resource-name class of lessence-gho: all three are one root cause, found while investigating 5m4. Kubernetes names resource types in reverse DNS by design (cephclusters.ceph.rook.io, postgresqls.acid.zalan.do, drivers.csi.ceph.io), so they are syntactically indistinguishable from hostnames. src/patterns/network.rs:231 decides with a hardcoded COMMON_TLDS list, which is why .io resources get erased to <FQDN> and .do ones survive — a coincidence, not a design. Proved it by running the RBAC corpus with --disable-patterns network: all four resources reappear intact. I tried and rejected several general rules. Keeping the leftmost label breaks pod DNS (pod-abc123.default.svc.cluster.local would keep its volatile name). A label-count threshold misfires on deep subdomains. Suppressing FQDN detection inside quoted strings would break genuine 'failed to connect to db.example.com' messages. Every rule that works reduces to a vocabulary of resource kinds or of error phrasings, which is the speculative generality worth an explicit decision rather than my invention. Blast radius is small on standard corpora — only 12 output lines across all 24 examples carry <FQDN> — so the reference sweep cannot gate a change here and new fixtures would be needed. Options for the owner: 1. accept a context vocabulary (treat a dotted token as a resource when it precedes 'is forbidden' or follows resource=/kind=), 2. give k8s API resources their own detector and token, which is what this bead originally asked for, 3. leave it and close all three. I have no recommendation between 1 and 2 without knowing which direction you want the normalizer to grow.

title: normalize: klog file:line, systemd unit and auditd type= are event identity — anchor them
description:
Found by the 25-corpus study (2026-08-28). Correctness class: unrelated
incidents merge.

Some grammars put the event identity in a fixed position as a NAME:
klog's `file.go:NNN]`, systemd's `<unit>.service:`, auditd's `type=X`. It is
the grammar's equivalent of syslog's program name. lessence tokenises it
(<PATH>, <KEY_VALUE>) and similarity then merges across it.

1. apiserver_production: group of 301 = remote_available_controller.go:448
   (246) + controller.go:113 + status.go:71 + dispatcher.go:205 (a 2 KB
   AdmissionReview JSON) — four subsystems under the generic `"Unhandled
   Error" err=<ESCAPED_JSON>` wrapper. A second group of 114 merges
   status.go + finisher.go + writers.go:122 + writers.go:135.
2. epyc_7days_journalctl: `rke2-agent.service: Main process exited` (8) is
   absorbed into `containerd.service: Main process exited` (103,328). Two
   incidents, two root causes, one group whose template says rke2-agent.
3. linux_auditd: `type=USYS_CONFIG ... changing system time` merged with 25
   `type=PATH name="/usr/sbin/ip"` lines. auditd's only discriminator became
   <KEY_VALUE>.
4. microservices HPA: `deployment/order-service` absorbs
   `deployment/notification-service` under a literal template.

lessence-gho did exactly the right thing for request paths and PCI
addresses: an anchor (normalize.rs anchor_hash) is matched, never scored.
These three are the same idea.

## Acceptance

Three anchor patterns added to anchor_hash: `^type=\w+` at line start,
`\b\w+\.go:\d+\]`, and `^\S+\.(service|slice|scope|socket|timer):` after the
syslog envelope. The apiserver group of 301 becomes 4; journalctl's
rke2-agent lines get their own group; auditd USYS_CONFIG stays alone.

Anchors are hard rejects, so gate carefully: --diff on kubelet (klog, 70k
lines) and journalctl (73 MB) and confirm nothing that SHOULD fold across a
file:line stopped folding. The kubelet root-cause splits the study confirmed
as correct must be unchanged.

Corpus ##TODO: study-klog-file-line-is-identity, study-systemd-unit-is-
identity, study-auditd-type-is-identity.

title: sanitizer: decide the entity set and per-entity action surface
description:
Decide the user-facing surface before any detection work, because both sibling
tasks depend on the answer.

Today `--sanitize-pii` is a boolean. A boolean cannot say which kinds to cover
or how to treat each one, and every comparable tool (Presidio, Cloud DLP,
Datadog, Cribl, the OTel redaction processor) settled on a named entity set with
a per-entity action.

## To decide

1. Entity names. Proposed `{email, credential, host, ip}` — small on purpose.
2. Action names. Proposed `{redact, pseudonym}`.
3. Syntax. Options include a repeatable `--sanitize <entity>[:<action>]`, a
   levelled `--sanitize-pii=strict`, or config-only. Whichever is picked must
   leave a bare `--sanitize-pii` meaning exactly what it means today.
4. Whether the default set ever grows. Adding an entity to the default changes
   output for existing users, so it is a release-notes-visible decision.

## Constraints

1. Backward compatibility: a bare `--sanitize-pii` keeps today's exact output.
2. The masking must continue to reach rollup variation samples, not just the
   representative line. That already works and is the easiest thing to break.
3. The doc_contract test enforces that every flag appears in README (via
   `make docs`) and in the agent skill's references/flags.md.

## Done when

The flag surface is written down and agreed, with the default behaviour
unchanged. No detection code required.

title: normalize: lines over 64 tokens fall back to a comparison the code documents as broken
description:
Found 2026-08-25 while measuring the kubelookout k8s JSON fixture. Distinct
from lessence-8jb, and on that corpus it is the bigger effect.

Lines with more than `MAX_SIMILARITY_TOKENS` (64, `src/patterns/mod.rs:244`)
tokens fall back to a positional byte comparison that the codebase already
documents as broken for this exact case. Two otherwise-identical records that
differ in the LENGTH of one early value score near zero, because every
subsequent byte is shifted out of alignment, and so they never fold.

## The cliff

Identical inputs apart from the number of trailing identical fields:

    # 20 tokens, under the cap
    evt state=up       f0=v0 ... f19=v19     x3
    evt state=degraded f0=v0 ... f19=v19     x3
    -> ONE group, [+4 similar]

    # 70 tokens, over the cap
    evt state=up       f0=v0 ... f69=v69     x3
    evt state=degraded f0=v0 ... f69=v69     x3
    -> TWO groups

Nothing about the difference changed. Only the length of the identical tail.

## Already known in the code

`similarity_score` in src/normalize.rs carries this comment above the LCS path:

    Token-level LCS: tolerant of an inserted or removed token, which a
    positional comparison is not (one early insertion used to cascade into a
    near-zero score for otherwise identical lines).

The LCS path was introduced to fix precisely that cascade, but it is gated on
`SimTokens::Tokens`, and any line over 64 tokens is `SimTokens::Overflow`. So
long lines still get the comparison the comment describes as the bug.

## Scale on the fixture

`examples/k8s_json_sample.log` (632 real lines, argocd + tetragon + gitaly),
run as `--format json --sanitize-pii --min-collapse 3 --threads 1`:

1. 218 groups from 634 lines; 155 are singletons.
2. Those singletons average 4,923 characters and share only 64 distinct
   120-character prefixes — they agree at the head and diverge deep inside
   several KB of tail.
3. Sampled tetragon records are 14,521 / 14,530 / 14,543 / 14,552 characters
   and 564 whitespace tokens each: nearly nine times the cap, differing by
   about 30 bytes in 14.5 KB, and each one lands in its own group.

kubelookout's per-pod measurements agree: their worst survivors are
tetragon-l5cw4 at 55% and tetragon-fbkw6 at 28%, both large-record sources.

## Why the cap exists, and a cheaper option

The cap bounds the LCS dynamic program, which is O(n*m) in tokens. Raising it
to cover 564-token records would mean ~318k DP cells per comparison, against
every group in the buffer — not viable.

But positional bytes are not the only alternative. `are_similar` already
computes `multiset_intersection` over the sorted token-hash views as an exact
O(n) upper bound on the LCS. For overflow lines that same intersection, used
directly as a similarity ratio, would be order-insensitive, allocation-free,
linear, and immune to the shifting problem — strictly better than positional
bytes for the case that currently fails. It loses token ORDER, so it would
over-merge lines that are permutations of each other; for structured records
with stable key order that is a much smaller error than the present one.

## Acceptance

The 70-token case above folds exactly as the 20-token case does, and no
existing reference output regresses. Gate with the usual corpus and perf sweep,
and include the k8s JSON fixture, since the standard corpora are mostly short
plaintext lines that never reach the cap.
close_reason: multiset comparison for 64-4096 token lines, plus an ordered 4-token head guard

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Fixed in 65d046f. Lines between MAX_SIMILARITY_TOKENS (64) and a new MAX_MULTISET_TOKENS (4096) now keep their sorted token hashes and are compared as multisets instead of by byte position. Past 4096 the hashes are dropped and the positional path still applies, deliberately: truncating the set would let two records agreeing only on their first few thousand tokens score as identical, which is worse than the bug being fixed. One thing the plan in this bead missed: a multiset alone over-merges. It ignores order, so a several-hundred-token map[...] payload outvoted the words identifying the message, and on rancher_production 18 'Updating TLS secret for ...' lines were absorbed into an 'Active TLS secret ...' group. Caught by the reference sweep, not by tests. Fixed by additionally requiring the first four tokens to match in order — four because that is the conventional timestamp/level/component/first-word prefix. Measured lead=8 as strictly worse: it pulls JSON values into the identity and cost 25 extra groups on the k8s fixture (165 vs 140) with no extra separation. Results on examples/k8s_json_sample.log: 218 groups to 140, singletons 155 to 105, and 20 percent FASTER (0.24s vs 0.30s median over 9 alternating runs, non-overlapping ranges) because comparing 564 hashes beats scanning 14.5 KB of bytes. Perf on the other five corpora is unchanged and provably so: journalctl has ZERO lines over 64 tokens in 655103, so the new path is unreachable there and the plus/minus 3 percent swings across runs are thermal noise on a 13-second measurement. Reference sweep 168/175, all 7 diffs on the k8s fixture and all in the folding direction. Four regression tests added covering the cliff, the distinct-message guard, payload order-insensitivity, and the past-4096 fallback.

comments.author: jorgen

Fixture reproduced exactly: 218 groups / 155 singletons to 140 / 105, and distinct normalized templates equalled group count in both runs. Live 15-minute windows, installed 0.4.5 versus fa92a0c32, collector flags: tetragon-fbkw6 772 lines 110 templates to 8; tetragon-l5cw4 237 lines 29 templates to 4; argocd-application-controller-0 382 lines 115 to 115 unchanged. They also report the first-four-token order guard cost nothing visible on tetragon, which is the evidence I lacked when choosing MULTISET_LEAD on two corpora.

title: normalize: field-aware anchors for request paths, device addresses, and resource names
description: The real fix for audit finding P0-2 (152,923 lines where similarity merged meaningful field differences). The vm9 re-sweep proved the global threshold cannot do it: netbox /metrics-vs-/login splits only at 88, gpu PCI devices at 90, rancher clusterrepo names at 92, and those thresholds cost +86% to +327% output lines corpus-wide. 1. Make request paths, PCI/device addresses, and resource/object names anchor tokens that must match exactly for lines to group, per the audit recommendation (src/normalize.rs similarity path). 2. Boolean/state values (first=true/false) are already protected at the new default 83 and need anchors only if the default ever drops. 3. Success: the three remaining P0-2 cases split at default threshold with no measurable corpus-wide compression loss beyond the anchor effect itself. 4. Perf and output gated like all similarity changes.
close_reason: classes 1-2 shipped in 4800408; class 3 consolidated into lessence-c2f

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Two of three classes shipped (commit 4800408). Mechanism: LogLine gains an anchor hash taken from the RAW line before normalization erases the field, folded into the line hash so the folder's exact-hash group index cannot bypass it, plus an equality check in are_similar. Anchors are matched, never scored. Class 1 request targets: anchors on the route, with digit runs inside a segment collapsed. That detail is load-bearing — treating whole segments as literal cost 11 points of compression on nginx_sample (75 to 64 percent) before the digit rule went in. Class 2 PCI addresses: anchors on the full domain:bus:device.function. Results on the audit's own cases: NetBox 76529-line group labelled GET /metrics now splits 57411 /login/ plus 19118 /metrics, matching threshold-100 ground truth at the default threshold. GPU 27866-line IOMMU group now splits 13933 plus 13933, one per device. Cost: +5.22 percent output lines across the 24 example corpora, essentially all of it PCI enumeration on epyc_7days_journalctl; --summary --top 30 and --fit on that corpus are byte-identical because the added groups are 6-13 lines each. Compare that with the threshold alternative the vm9 sweep measured at +86 to +327 percent. Perf: journalctl is about 16 percent FASTER (median 13.02s vs 15.53s over 9 alternating runs) because spreading anchored lines over more distinct hashes routes more of them through the O(1) group index instead of the linear similarity scan; the other five corpora are unchanged. All 21 reference-output diffs are separations that were previously wrong, listed in the commit message. Still open: class 3, resource and object names (the rancher clusterrepo case, still one 21440-line group). Every rule I could find for it reduces to a vocabulary of resource kinds, which is the kind of speculative generality worth an explicit owner decision rather than an invented heuristic. Note also that anchors are asymmetric by design: a line carrying an anchor never groups with one that carries none. That is what stopped nginx health checks merging with kubelet lines at --threshold 60.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Class 3 (resource and object names) is blocked on the same root cause as lessence-5m4 and lessence-c2f, both now marked blocked with the full analysis on c2f. Short version: k8s resource types are reverse-DNS by design and so are syntactically identical to hostnames; network.rs erases them via a hardcoded TLD list. No syntactic anchor rule can separate them, so class 3 needs the same owner decision as those two. Classes 1 and 2 (request targets, PCI addresses) are shipped in 4800408.

title: Escape untrusted log content in --format markdown output
description:
src/main.rs:564-568 — the markdown emitter writes untrusted log content without escaping. Non-folded entries are written raw via format!("{output}\n") (main.rs:568) with no fence; folded entries sit in a bare three-backtick fence (main.rs:564-566) that a content line containing three backticks closes early. Content originates verbatim from group.first().original / line.original.clone() (folder.rs:1245/1265/1308). No markdown/HTML escaping, fence-length escalation, or backtick stripping exists anywhere in src/.

Impact: a crafted log line injects markdown structure (headings, links, images) or breaks out of the code fence when the report is rendered (e.g. GitHub) or ingested by an LLM/coding agent. GitHub sanitizes active script (not full XSS) but renders attacker links/images/headings.

Fix:
1. HTML/markdown-escape non-folded content, or always wrap it in a fence.
2. For fenced blocks, use a backtick run longer than any in the content (CommonMark allows longer fences) or strip/escape backtick runs and control chars first.
3. Combine with the terminal-escape sanitizer (the strip_ansi_codes fix) so raw ESC/OSC bytes are not carried into the report.

Provenance: threat-model -> vuln-scan -> triage; confirmed TRUE_POSITIVE 3/0, confidence 8.7/10; severity MEDIUM. See TRIAGE.md (F-005).

title: normalize: eight value shapes still fold by length or charset (8jb follow-up)
description:
Found by the 25-corpus study (2026-08-28). lessence-8jb fixed JSON numbers
and DNS labels; these are the shapes it did not cover, each measured.

The signature is `--explain nearest.score` of exactly 80.0 or 81.8 across
corpora: one token differs on a short line and the threshold is 83.

1. Bare logfmt `key=<1-2 digit int>`: `partition=0`, `attempt_count=1`
   (microservices), `entries=6` (auditd). 8jb rejected the logfmt half on the
   auditd SYSCALL over-merge; this study shows the cost on 4 corpora. A
   narrower rule: fold `key=<int>` only when the same key carries a
   DIFFERENT int on another line in the batch — never in prose.
2. Small int in a prose position: `error state 6|7` (apache), `PacketResponder
   0|1|2` (hdfs), `slot 7` (apache-error, folds but lies), thread id `27`
   vs `28` in a positional column (hdfs). \d{3,} decides by digit count.
3. auditd `audit(1481076985.580:66)`: the `:66` sequence counter is not
   tokenised. 324 NETFILTER_CFG boot lines → 306 groups (294 singletons).
   The whole `audit(<epoch>.<ms>:<seq>)` is one record id.
4. k8s 5-char pod suffix when the preceding chunk is already a token:
   `gitlab-sidekiq-all-in-1-v2-6cf6f474bd-7j5z7` → `...-<HASH>-7j5z7`.
   HYPHENATED_NAMES cannot match after the replacement. kubectl-events
   (5/3 asymmetric split), kubelet (reconciler singletons), cilium
   (endpoint lifecycle → 49 groups instead of ~6, one singleton at 82.8).
5. `kube-api-access-qgnbg` → `kube-api-access-<SUFFIX>qgnbg`: the
   COMMON_PREFIXES path in names.rs:52 leaves residue → 3,147 kubelet lines
   never fold. Real bug, not a threshold case.
6. Non-hex `*_id=` values: trace_id `5af93g46...`, container_id
   `def456ghi789`. A 12–32 char [a-z0-9] value in an id field folds
   whatever its charset (synthetic corpora, but the rule is real).
7. `resourceName="devices.kubevirt.io/tun"` vs `nvidia.com/gpu`: 4 groups;
   and `Adding GroupVersion autoscaling v2` stays out of a 124-line group
   because the others have a dotted name → <FQDN> and it does not.
8. NCSA bytes-sent `490` vs `3316` (nginx, 81.8): a 3-digit and a 4-digit
   int score differently in the LCS because token LENGTH is compared, not
   token class.

## Acceptance

Each numbered shape gets a ##CASE from the corpus ##TODO list and folds.
Item 5 first (it is a plain bug). Items 3 and 4 are single new shapes.
Item 1 needs the narrow rule stated above and a --diff on auditd proving
SYSCALL records for different syscalls still stay apart.

Corpus ##TODO: study-auditd-record-id-is-one-token, study-small-int-in-
prose-folds, study-logfmt-small-int-folds, study-pod-suffix-after-hash-folds.

comments.author: jorgen
comments.text: Reviewed, not implemented — the bead itself calls this a pure product proposal for the owner to scope or reject, and nothing in it can be settled by measurement alone. One correction to the framing: the audit's example (a 5208-line RBAC-failure group ranked 161st) is a whole-lab-corpus ranking, not a per-file one. Within its own source, 137.log, that group is the LARGEST and ranks first by frequency, so frequency ranking surfaces it fine when a user runs lessence on the log they are actually investigating. The 161st ranking only appears when 580 sources are ranked together, where health probes and metrics scrapes dominate. That weakens the motivating example but not necessarily the idea: the real argument for anomaly ranking is that severity, novelty and state changes are better relevance signals than count, which stands independently. Recommend the owner decide whether that is a product they want before any scoping work, since the design space (severity, novelty, state changes, cross-pod spread, restart correlation, per the bead) is wide and each signal needs its own definition and its own corpus evidence. comments.text: Recommend rejecting in the proposed form. Measured the premise on two real single-log corpora instead of the concatenated lab set. kubelet.log: 179 groups, the top 3 by frequency ARE the incident (rpc error, failed to setup network for sandbox), and the largest error-level groups rank 5, 8 and 9 — all inside a default --top 30. epyc_7days_journalctl: 1906 groups, top 3 by frequency are the real incident (rke2-agent.service crash loop, 103337 lines each), highest error-level group ranks 25, next ranks 91 with 9 lines. title: Hoist per-line context decisions out of key-value per-match closures (O(N^2) to O(N))
description:
src/patterns/key_value.rs — detect_and_replace runs four regex replace_all passes, each calling a full-line helper inside its per-match closure: is_metrics_context (line 68, to_lowercase at 239), is_config_context (88, to_lowercase at 258), is_logging_json (111, about 10 contains at 279-281), is_valid_key_value_context (131, to_uppercase 4 times plus contains at 301-307). Short repeating key=value tokens produce Theta(N) matches, each doing Theta(N) full-line work, giving Theta(N^2).

Impact: a single line (up to the 1 MB default cap) of repeated a=1 tokens that passes has_key_value_indicators (48-59) drives roughly 10^11 to 10^12 operations plus heavy allocation churn — a multi-second-to-minute single-thread stall, repeatable per line. Reachable via normalize.rs:131 for any line containing = or :.

Fix:
1. Compute the line-level decisions (is_metrics_context, is_config_context, is_logging_json, and the SQL/math/uppercase exclusions) once per line before replace_all.
2. Pass the cached booleans/strings into the closures; keep only the key/value checks per-match.
3. Optionally cap match count per line.

Provenance: threat-model -> vuln-scan -> triage; confirmed TRUE_POSITIVE 3/0, confidence 7.7/10; severity MEDIUM (scan claimed HIGH, re-rated down one: bounded by the 1 MB cap, not unbounded). Absorbs F-010 (key_value.rs:301) and F-011 (key_value.rs:111). See TRIAGE.md (F-002).
close_reason: Line-level checks hoisted to once per pass (exact semantics preserved); 15x speedup on 200KB repro, quadratic blowup eliminated

title: normalize: whole-line keyword sniffs change how unrelated fields tokenise
description:
Found by the 25-corpus study (2026-08-28). Confirmed on 4 corpora.

KeyValueDetector decides per LINE whether to run its config/metrics/json
passes, via whole-line keyword sniffs: is_config_context() (key_value.rs:219)
scans for "config", "configuration", "settings", "params", "options",
"environment"...; is_metrics_context() and is_logging_json() likewise. A word
anywhere in the line changes how an unrelated field tokenises.

1. openssh_brute_force line 2476: the attacker tried username "config".
   That one word flips `sshd[3581664]:` from `sshd[pid=<PID>]:` to
   `sshd[<KEY_VALUE>` (the `]:` is eaten). nearest.score 80.0 → the line
   splits from 11,318 identical siblings. Whether a brute-force line folds
   depends on which username was guessed.
2. cilium_full: reason="Configuration or devices changed" — the WORD
   Configuration trips the sniff; CONFIG_KV_REGEX then eats `time="`,
   `level=info`, `msg="regenerating` and the word itself. Template becomes
   `<KEY_VALUE> <KEY_VALUE> <KEY_VALUE> all endpoints<QUOTED_STRING>
   <KEY_VALUE>`; 19 lines land next to a --config flag line at 72.7 instead
   of their 15,084-line sibling.
3. linux_auditd: `audit(1481077254.276:518)` → <TIMESTAMP> on most lines but
   <DECIMAL> on 51 groups, depending on what else is on the line.
4. enhanced_timestamps: has_timestamp_indicators() (detector.rs:276) requires
   a ':' in the line, so the `@epoch` pattern (detector.rs:196) is
   unreachable. A pattern that ships but can never fire.

This is the lessence-8jb principle applied to the other detectors: the
decision belongs to the match, not the line.

## Acceptance

Delete the whole-line context sniffs in key_value.rs (config/metrics/json)
and the ':' precondition in has_timestamp_indicators(). Each regex decides
on its own match. The two openssh lines above normalise identically; the
cilium reason keeps the word Configuration; `@1758304800.311` → <TIMESTAMP>.

Gate with --diff on all 25 corpora. Expect kubelet/cilium/apiserver to move
(they are logfmt-heavy); every move must be explainable as "the line no
longer depends on a keyword elsewhere".

Corpus ##TODO: study-config-word-does-not-change-tokenising,
study-configuration-word-is-not-eaten, study-epoch-at-prefix-without-colon.
close_reason: whole-line keyword sniffs and the dash veto removed; each regex decides per match
